Rashi on Makkot 24a:10:1.hebrew: נבזה בעיניו נמאס - הנמאס להקב"ה נבזה הוא בעיניו של אדם. ואיזהו? זה חזקיהו, שנבזה היה בעיניו אביו שנמאס בעבודת כוכבים:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:10:1.english: “In whose eyes a vile person is despised” - One who is despised by the Holy One, blessed be He, is vile in this person’s eyes. And who is this? This is Hezekiah, in whose eyes his father was vile, because he was despised on account of idolatry.

Rashi on Makkot 24a:10:2.hebrew: שגיררו במטה של חבלים - גמרא היא, ולא קרא (וקורא לו רבי רבי):
Rashi on Makkot 24a:10:2.english: That he dragged him on a bed of ropes - This is the language of the Gemara, and it is not [part of] the verse: (“and he calls him ‘Rabbi, Rabbi’”)

Rashi on Makkot 24a:13:1.hebrew: ואפילו לעובד כוכבים - כדי שלא ימשוך ויבוא להלוות לישראל ברבית:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:13:1.english: And even to a gentile - So that he not be drawn after it and come to lend to a Jew with interest.

Rashi on Makkot 24a:14:1.hebrew: שוחד על נקי לא לקח - אפילו שוחד שהיה רשאי ליקח:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:14:1.english: “Nor takes a bribe against the innocent” - Even a bribe that he was permitted to take.

Rashi on Makkot 24a:14:2.hebrew: כגון ישמעאל ברבי יוסי - שהיה אריסו מביא לו משלו פירות [קודם זמנו], ולא רצה ליקח כדי להיות לו דיין:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:14:2.english: Such as Yishmael the son of Rabbi Yosei - For his sharecropper would bring him some of his own [produce] [before its time], and he did not want to accept it, so that he could be a judge for him.

Rashi on Makkot 24a:17:1.hebrew: בבצע מעשקות - שלא רצה ליטול לעצמו ראשית הגז שהביא לו אדם אחד שבא לדון לפניו, אע"ג דהוה כהן — רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע — משום דדמי כאילו עושקו לכהן שהיה רגיל זה ליתן לו מתנותיו:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:17:1.english: The gain of oppressions - [This refers to one] who did not want to take for himself the first shearing of the fleece that a certain man, who had come to be judged before him, brought him — even though he was a priest, [as was] Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha — because it is considered as though he were defrauding the priest [of his due], since this man was accustomed to give him his priestly gifts.

Rashi on Makkot 24a:17:2.hebrew: אוטם אזנו משמוע דמים - אזנו חתומה וסתומה בדבר זה, שלא ישמע בה דבר גנאי ושותק. והיינו "דמים", לשון שתיקה:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:17:2.english: Who stops his ears from hearing blood - His ear is sealed and stopped up regarding this matter, so that he does not hear in it a disgraceful thing and remain silent. And this is [the meaning of] "blood" (damim) — an expression of silence.

Rashi on Makkot 24a:1:1.hebrew: שית מאה וחד סרי - והיינו דכתיב ״תורה צוה לנו משה״, ושתים מפי הגבורה, הרי הן שית מאה ותליסרי:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:1:1.english: Six hundred and eleven - And this is what is written, "Moses commanded us the Torah" (Deuteronomy 33:4); and two [were heard] from the mouth of the Almighty. Behold, they are six hundred and thirteen.

Rashi on Makkot 24a:1:2.hebrew: מפי הגבורה שמענום - דכתיב (תהלים סב, יב) אחת דבר אלהים, ושתים זו שמענו. כך למדנו במכילתא:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:1:2.english: From the mouth of the Almighty we heard them - As it is written: "God has spoken once; two things have I heard" — [that is,] these two we heard [directly]. We learned this in the Mechilta.

Rashi on Makkot 24a:22:1.hebrew: כגון רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון - בהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ דף פד:), דנפק ריחשא מאודניה, ואיתחזי לאיתתיה בחלמא, ואמר לה: האי דשמעית בזילותא דצורבא מרבנן ולא מחאי כדמבעי לי. אלמא, בחייו הוה רגיל לדקדק בכך, ולפיכך הקפיד הקב"ה עליו על אותו הפעם שלא מיחה:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:22:1.english: Such as Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon - In [the chapter] "Hasocher et HaPoalim" (Bava Metzia, p. 84b), [where it says] that a worm emerged from his ear, and he appeared to his wife in a dream and said to her: "That which I heard the disparagement of a Torah scholar and did not protest as I ought." Evidently, during his lifetime he was accustomed to be scrupulous about this, and therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, took issue with him over that one time that he did not protest.

Rashi on Makkot 24a:26:1.hebrew: זו הוצאת המת והכנסת הכלה - דכתיב בהו (קהלת ז, ב) "לכת טוב ללכת אל בית אבל מלכת וגו'":
Rashi on Makkot 24a:26:1.english: This is taking out the dead and bringing in the bride - For it is written regarding them: "It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, etc." (Ecclesiastes 7:2).

Rashi on Makkot 24a:27:1.hebrew: בא ישעיה בן אמוץ - כל שעה היו דורות שבאו של מטה והיו מתמעטין:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:27:1.english: Isaiah son of Amoz came - With every passing hour, the generations below [i.e., later generations] were diminishing [in their ability to observe the mitzvot].

Rashi on Makkot 24a:28:1.hebrew: חדל נא - אותה ברכה שאמר משה "וישכון ישראל בטח בדד עין יעקב", כלומר: אימתי ישכון ישראל בטח? כשיהיו צדיקים כעין יעקב:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:28:1.english: Cease, I beseech You - [Amos was referring to] that blessing that Moses said, "And Israel dwells in safety, the fountain of Jacob alone"; that is to say, when will Israel dwell in safety? When they are righteous, in the likeness [ein] of Jacob.

Rashi on Makkot 24a:28:2.hebrew:
מי יקום יעקב - מי יוכל להיות חסיד כיעקב, כי קטן הוא; קטנים הם הטובים שיהיו צדיקים כיעקב:
[מכאן ואילך מפרש רבינו גרשום]:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:28:2.english:
How shall Jacob stand - Who can be pious like Jacob? For he is small; the small ones are the good ones, who can be righteous like Jacob.
[From here on, Rabbeinu Gershom explains]:

Rashi on Makkot 24a:3:1.hebrew: והעמידן על אחת עשרה - שבתחלה היו צדיקים, והיו יכולים לקבל עול מצות הרבה. אבל דורות האחרונים לא היו צדיקים כל כך, ואם באו לשמור כולן, אין לך אדם שזוכה. ובא דוד והעמידן כו' כדי שיזכו, אם יקיימו י"א מצות הללו. וכן כל שעה, דורות של מטה הולכין וממעטין אותו:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:3:1.english: And he established them upon eleven - For at first [the generations] were righteous, and they were able to accept the yoke of many commandments. But the later generations were not so righteous, and if they came to observe all of them, there would be no person who merits [the World-to-Come]. And David came and established them, etc., so that they would merit if they fulfill these eleven commandments. And so, at every time, the lower [i.e., later] generations go and reduce it:

Rashi on Makkot 24a:6:1.hebrew: רב ספרא - בשאלתות דרב אחא (שאילתא לו). והכי הוה עובדא דרב ספרא: היה לו חפץ אחד למכור, ובא אדם אחד לפניו בשעה שהיה קורא ק"ש, ואמר לו: תן לי החפץ בכך וכך דמים, ולא ענהו מפני שהיה קורא ק"ש. כסבור זה שלא היה רוצה ליתנו בדמים הללו, והוסיף. אמר: תנהו לי בכך יותר. לאחר שסיים ק"ש אמר לו: טול החפץ בדמים שאמרת בראשונה, שבאותן דמים היה דעתי ליתנם לך:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:6:1.english: Rav Safra - [This is found] in the She'iltot of Rav Acha (She'ilta 36). And this is how the incident of Rav Safra occurred: He had a certain item to sell, and a certain man came before him while he was reciting Shema, and said to him: "Give me the item for such-and-such a price," but [Rav Safra] did not answer him because he was reciting Shema. [The buyer] thought that [Rav Safra] was not willing to give it for that price, and he added. He said: "Give it to me for this higher amount." After [Rav Safra] finished Shema, he said to him: "Take the item for the price you stated at first, for it was my intention to give it to you for that price."

Rashi on Makkot 24a:7:1.hebrew: (אף) לא רגל על לשונו [כו'] - לא רצה לשקר מתחלה, שאמר "אולי ימושני [אבי]"; אלא שאמו הכריחתו ועל פי הדבור, דכתיב "עלי קללתך בני", ומתרגמינן "אלי אתאמר בנבואה [דלא ייתון לווטיא עלך ברי]":
Rashi on Makkot 24a:7:1.english: (Also) "He did not slander with his tongue" [etc.] - He did not want to lie at the outset, as he said, "Perhaps my father will feel me [my father]"; rather, his mother compelled him, and it was by divine word, as it is written, "Upon me be your curse, my son," which we translate [in the Targum] as "It was told to me in prophecy [that the curses will not come upon you, my son]."

Rashi on Makkot 24a:9:1.hebrew: וחרפה לא נשא על קרובו - לא סבל חרפת קרובו:
Rashi on Makkot 24a:9:1.english: “Nor takes up reproach against his relative” - He did not tolerate the disgrace of his relative.
